title: Ad for Netflix on Bing leads to tech support scam
description: Scammers are buying ad space on popular search engines to lead people to their company. Beware. Read more at http://mwb.to/NetflixScam2

textual.observation: The source describes an ad for Netflix on Bing leading viewers to a company's destination, and identifies the described mechanism as a tech support scam.

evidence.quote: Ad for Netflix on Bing leads to tech support scam
Scammers are buying ad space on popular search engines to lead people to their company.

textual.context: Presented as a warning/reporting description; the records do not establish whether the speaker endorses or independently verified the claim.
textual.potential_relevance: The relationship between a Netflix-related search ad and a destination described as the company's site, together with the stated tech-support-scam mechanism, is a concretely described pathway for later contextual assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not specify the audience's requested action, any payment or data request, the destination's identity, or whether anyone experienced a loss.

visual.observation: A search result and a webpage present telephone support for Netflix, including a prominently displayed toll-free number and a request to call or request a callback. The webpage labels the service "Affiliated Help" and displays Netflix branding.
visual.context: The page visibly presents itself as customer support, but its relationship to Netflix is qualified by an on-page disclaimer.
visual.potential_relevance: A claimed Netflix-support identity is linked to directing viewers to make contact by telephone or callback request, which conditionally merits review.
visual.limitations: These frames cannot establish whether the phone number connects to Netflix, who operates the service, whether anyone was contacted, or what occurred afterward.

visual.observation: A Windows User Account Control dialog asks whether to allow "Ammyy Admin" to make changes to the computer, while a page behind it describes remote desktop software and remote desktop connection.
visual.context: The frame shows a software authorization prompt and remote-desktop-related interface; the surrounding purpose and speaker request are unclear.
visual.potential_relevance: An authorization step for remote-desktop software is visibly connected to allowing a program downloaded from the internet to make changes to the computer, which conditionally merits review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame cannot establish who initiated the authorization, whether it was accepted, what access was obtained, or whether it was connected to the earlier support presentation.

textual_context_notes.observation: The description explicitly warns viewers about the described search-ad pathway.

visual_context_notes.observation: The support webpage states that it is an independent technical support service, is not connected to the brands it supports, and provides a disclaimer that it is not an authorized service.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a warning or report about a Netflix-related search advertisement leading to a technical-support destination. The visuals demonstrate the reported pathway, including an unauthorized independent support page and a remote-desktop authorization prompt, rather than inviting viewers to use the service. the available video evidence does not establish who operated the service, whether the prompt was accepted, or whether anyone suffered a loss.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary theme is warning about and examining a purported technical-support scam pathway, rather than promoting participation in it. The warning language is explicit, and the frames show the support destination and remote-access prompt as investigation subject matter.

evidence.observation: The title describes an investigation or report about a Netflix-related Bing advertisement leading to a technical-support scam.

evidence.observation: A webpage visibly presents 'Affiliated Help', 'Help & Support for NETFLIX Videos', a telephone number, 'Request For Callback', and 'Chat with us'; the page also visibly includes a disclaimer describing the service as independent and not connected with the brands it supports.
A Windows User Account Control dialog visibly asks whether to allow 'Ammyy Admin' to make changes to the computer, with a remote-desktop webpage visible behind it.
